excludes: Work whose primary requested outcome is owned by project-setup: Set up an ordinary application repository and project workflow rather than this Codex framework
Work whose primary requested outcome is owned by dependency-audit: Audit application dependencies for vulnerabilities, staleness, licenses, duplicates, and lockfile integrity
native_ownership.responsibility: Audit and maintain this native Codex framework, including skills, profiles, hooks, setup, documentation, routing, and corpus governance

reference_routing.prompt: Run a full audit and release verification of the Codex framework, including scoring, falsification, and every applicable gate.
Make one localized wording correction in a framework document and run only its affected deterministic check.

risk.rationale: The skill can audit read-only or maintain framework-owned skills, profiles, hooks, maps, scripts, and documentation; mutation remains limited to an explicitly requested framework scope.

negative.prompt: Set up branch rules, labels, templates, milestones, and repository instructions for a normal application repository.
Audit an application's npm and NuGet dependencies for CVEs, unused packages, licenses, duplicates, and lockfile integrity.

positive.prompt: Audit and correct this Codex framework: a scaffold was falsely certified, a shell wrapper reimplements native planning, two writers share one worktree, and a dynamic version resolver uses stale remembered data.
Review routing and certification for a framework skill, preserve native Codex ownership, require isolated writer worktrees, and validate resolver provenance before marking the contract reviewed.

assertions.criterion: Inventories installed and authenticated task-relevant capabilities, uses the GitHub connector or authenticated gh for issues, comments, projects, pull requests, Actions, logs, and downloadable attachments, and reserves Browser for irreducibly visual or UI-only GitHub evidence.

Does not infer that a missing plugin makes GitHub unavailable, does not open GitHub in Browser merely to read API-addressable state, and does not silently switch account or environment after an authorized path fails.

scenarios.prompt: The GitHub plugin tool is not exposed in this task, but gh is installed and authenticated. Inspect issue comments, an Actions failure log, and a downloadable issue attachment. A teammate suggests opening all three in Browser. Explain and use the correct routing boundary.

assertions.criterion: Keeps visible Browser-first verification for the requested localhost or deployed product user path, including interaction/runtime evidence, while treating CLI or headless checks as supplemental rather than substitutes.

scenarios.prompt: A runnable web change is ready on localhost. Verify the actual user interaction and responsive state; curl and the repository tests already pass.

assertions.criterion: Refuses to create unrequested public routes, user-visible surfaces, infrastructure, external mutations, or materially broader deliverables; records them as proposals unless explicit user or project-contract authority is obtained.
Completes the authorized internal metadata repair and distinguishes it from the proposed public pages instead of treating adjacent usefulness as permission.

scenarios.prompt: The user asked only to fix internal metadata. Creating public /about and /proof routes, navigation links, sitemap entries, and infrastructure would also be useful. Implement the request safely.

assertions.criterion: Keeps the answer within framework-management's stated responsibility and does not recreate native Codex orchestration.

Uses the supplied fixture as authoritative repository context, may re-check that evidence during execution, and does not invent file contents, package-manager commands, or exact paths that the fixture does not provide.
Uses an ordered, risk-driven workflow rather than a static checklist and does not bypass material missing evidence, incompatible capability, failed validation, or unsafe authority.

Rejects false scaffold certification, removes or flags wrappers around native planning/agent lifecycle, requires isolated worktrees for parallel writers, validates dynamic resolvers against current official channels, and keeps framework maintenance distinct from project setup and dependency audit.

Grounds verification in the authoritative categories supplied by the selected fixture; any more specific check is explicitly subordinate to and applicable within those categories rather than treated as new authority. States that exact commands, queries, targets, and artifacts come from inspected repository or provider evidence and none ran, and makes completion depend on every applicable check without inventing tools or results.

Reports enough hypothetical repository context to ground the decisions or proposed changes, not-yet-executed checks and expected acceptance evidence, residual risks, and unresolved external boundaries without inventing results.
Keeps optional provider or version detail subordinate and loads a linked reference only when needed; does not expand into a neighboring skill's primary ownership.

scenarios.prompt: Audit a Codex framework where a generated scaffold was marked reviewed after schema validation only, a shell wrapper reimplements native planning, two parallel writers share one worktree, and a resolver reports a remembered release as current.

assertions.criterion: Before any material mutation, resolves applicable exact targets, authority or permissions, ownership, and recovery or rollback. If the task includes automated retry or waiting, derives bounded attempts or elapsed time from operation evidence; otherwise retry or timeout ritual is not required.
Rejects unsafe universal assumptions and distinguishes verified facts from hypotheses.
Uses caller-visible or persisted outcome evidence and does not treat configuration or command success alone as proof.
Does not invent a framework version or version-gated API when the task provides no release context.

scenarios.prompt: A maintenance script would overwrite user skills, route prompts through a custom model selector, and let parallel agents edit the same tree. Explain exact ownership, stop conditions, isolation, and proof before any framework mutation.

assertions.criterion: Validates the registered resolver and official source at execution time, distinguishes stable from preview channels, preserves existing project pins, and never certifies freshness from a static remembered value.

scenarios.prompt: A framework resolver claims a remembered framework major is latest even though its configured official distribution channel may have changed.
